9.heading: Babel:
refs: that is, Confusion, The tower of Babel, Herodotus informs us, was a furlong or 660 feet, in length and breadth

and, according to Strabo, it rose to the same altitude. It was of a pyramidical form, consisting of eight square towers, gradually decreasing in breadth, with a winding ascent on the outside, so very broad as to allow horses and carriages to pass each other, and even to turn. This magnificent structure is so completely destroyed that its very site is doubtful
and when supposed to be discovered, in all cases exhibiting a heap of rubbish. Gen 10:5 , 10 , 20 , 31

29.heading: Sarai:
refs: Iscah is called the daughter-in-law of Terah - Gen 11:31
yet Abram afterwards said, "she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother" - Gen 20:12 . Probably Haran was the eldest son of Terah, and Abram his youngest by another wife
and thus Sarai was the daughter, or grand-daughter of Terah, Abram's father, but not of his mother.

Iscah:
Iscah is called the daughter-in-law of Terah - Gen 11:31 ; as being Abram's wife; yet Abram afterwards said, "she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother" - Gen 20:12 . Probably Haran was the eldest son of Terah, and Abram his youngest by another wife; and thus Sarai was the daughter, or grand-daughter of Terah, Abram's father, but not of his mother.
